ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an operational amplifier inverting proportional calculation circuit. The input signal ui is connected to the inverting input terminal of the op-amp through the input resistor R1; the feedback resistor Rf is connected back from the output terminal to the inverting input terminal; the non-inverting input terminal is grounded through the resistor R2, and the output terminal is labeled uo. Reasoning: The voltage gain of the inverting proportional operation circuit is uo/ui = -Rf/R1. The problem gives ui = 10cos400t mV, uo = -200cos400t mV, therefore uo/ui = (-200cos400t)/(10cos400t) = -20. Let -Rf/R1 = -20, obtaining Rf/R1 = 20, so Rf = 20R1.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as an ideal op-amp with negative feedback: the plus input is tied to ground via R2, so the minus input node is at virtual ground. The input current is i1 = u_i/R1 and cannot enter the op-amp, so it must flow through Rf to the output: i_f = -u_o/Rf. Equate currents, u_i/R1 = -u_o/Rf. Substitute the text values u_i = 10 cos 400t mV and u_o = -200 cos 400t mV; the common cos 400t and mV cancel, giving 10/R1 = 200/Rf, so Rf = 20R1.
